summary: NDR feed s175_triple is degraded with 3 faults: tool overload (34.02 Gbps burst on 10 Gbps port, 340% capacity), 8.5% duplicates, and 94.4% encrypted share exceeding 90% NDR tolerance. No packet drops, one-way, or VLAN issues detected.

findings.root_cause: 1ms microburst peaked at 34.02 Gbps on a 10 Gbps NDR port (340% of capacity, 1 overloaded interval). Packet broker is aggregating too much traffic onto a single tool port without load balancing, causing drops at the NDR NIC even though broker shows no drops.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR will drop packets at ingress during bursts, causing incomplete flow reassembly and missed detections. NDR needs both directions and full payload, so any tool-side loss creates blind spots.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute 34 Gbps bursts across multiple 10G NDR ports to keep per-port utilization <80% and prevent tool-side drops

findings.root_cause: 8.5% duplicates (706 of 8354 packets, threshold 5%) indicates same packets arriving via multiple SPAN/mirror paths or overlapping TAP aggregation without broker deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: Wastes ~8.5% of NDR processing and 10G bandwidth on redundant packets, inflates flow counts, skews NDR analytics, and worsens the overload condition.

recommended_fix.why: Remove duplicates at packet broker before delivery to free NDR capacity and correct analytics

findings.root_cause: 94.4% of bytes are encrypted vs NDR tolerance of 90%. Traffic is predominantly TLS without visibility-layer decryption, leaving only headers for inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for deep inspection; with 94% encrypted it is blind to payload content, severely limiting detection of malware, C2 and exfiltration inside encrypted sessions.

params.solution: out-of-band SSL visibility appliance or selective decryption policy

recommended_fix.why: NDR cannot inspect encrypted payload at this share; decrypt relevant TLS at visibility layer or tune NDR to focus on metadata/JA3/JA4 and encrypted-traffic analytics
